agreed.amal_said: الصباح. either الصباح or في الصباح.
agreed.why: Bare صباح for 'in the morning'; Amal recast with el- (or في الصباح) and he repeated في الصباح.
agreed.english: I had an important client in the morning.

agreed.why: He said خريف (autumn) for lamb; Amal echoed خريف questioningly and he switched to خروف, then she asked what خريف means.

agreed.amal_said: واحدة. Because it's ساعة... الساعة واحدة or just واحدة.
agreed.why: Clock time takes the feminine number (الساعة واحدة); he said واحد twice and Amal corrected to واحدة, explaining it's because of ساعة.

agreed.amal_said: بؤ. Eh, on it... عليه بقع.
agreed.why: He said the shirt عنده (has) stains; Amal said 'on it' and recast عليه بقع (بوع is just the ق-as-hamza pronunciation of بقع, S4).
Talking about what he already did, he used present بحط; Amal supplied past حطيت and he said 'Oh, that's right. أنا حطيت'.

agreed.medi_said: Do I know the word for beets? ... أنا نسيت الـ...
agreed.why: He asked for beets and Amal supplied بنجر (sheet: beet | Banjar | بنجر).

agreed.medi_said: wait for you would be ستنت لك، ستنيت لك،
agreed.why: Object 'you' rides on the verb, not on لـ; Amal recast استنيتك and he took it ('There's no il').

agreed.medi_said: حكيت لي، آآآ، حكيت-- حكيت لي ني؟
agreed.why: He stacked -ni onto لي ('حكيت لي ني'); Amal said No, try again, then gave حكيت لي.

agreed.amal_said: هلأ قصدك إنه أغلب ما بتحتاج ال
agreed.why: Negating a verb with مش; Amal restated his sentence with ما بتحتاج.

agreed.medi_said: How do you say my clothes? Is it أَوَا...
agreed.why: He asked how to say my clothes; Amal supplied it (sheet: clothes (plural) | Awaa3i | أواعي).

agreed.amal_said: Why ال آخر؟ / آخر الأسبوع صح، بس مش ال آخر الأسبوع. أغلب آخر الأسبوع.
agreed.why: In the chain أغلب + آخر + الأسبوع only the last noun takes el-; Amal asked why ال آخر and gave أغلب آخر الأسبوع.
He flipped the idafa order; Amal recast أغلب آخر الأسبوع and he repeated it.
انبسط takes بـ for what you enjoyed; Amal gave بالشط and he said 'I forgot about انبسط' and fixed to بالشاطئ.

agreed.amal_said: شو الأول؟ What's feminine of أول؟ ... بدلة.
agreed.why: Engine wrote الأولى but Amal's echo شو الأول؟ shows he said الأول with feminine بدلة; he fixed to أولى.
He used أكثر (most) for 'best'; Amal pushed 'best/better' and he said أحسن إشي.

agreed.amal_said: Ahsan. One. Now, what does one mean?
agreed.why: For 'the best one' he used إشي (thing); Amal prompted 'one' and he built أحسن واحدة (feminine for لبسة).
agreed.proposed_rule: 'The X one' = superlative/ordinal + واحد/واحدة matching the noun's gender, not إشي: آخر لبسة كانت أحسن واحدة; نفس أول واحد.

agreed.amal_said: It's not idafa here, it's just adjective... You're missing an L.
agreed.why: Noun + adjective phrase needs el- on both; Amal said 'you're missing an L' and he fixed to الكندرة الأخيرة.
'The beginning of my day' needs the possessive ending, not el-; Amal prompted and he said أول يومي, she said صح.
'My whole day' needs the possessive ending; Amal repeated 'My whole day' and he said كل يومي.
For 'boring' he reused يزعل (saddening); Amal gave بيزهق (sheet: boring / causes boredom | beyzahheq | بيزهق).
agreed.english: The end of the lesson was boring.

agreed.why: He used العربية (Arabic language / fem.) for 'Arabs'; Amal gave the people plural العرب / العربيين.

agreed.amal_said: أول شو؟ ... What's one? What's one?
agreed.why: 'The same as the first one' left out واحد; Amal asked أول شو / what's one and he added واحد.
agreed.english: the same as the first one
agreed.proposed_rule: 'The X one' = superlative/ordinal + واحد/واحدة matching the noun's gender, not إشي: آخر لبسة كانت أحسن واحدة; نفس أول واحد.

agreed.why: He said قبل ما (before) for 'after'; Amal said 'After' and he switched to ba'id ma.
Wrong person on the past verb (I saw for we saw); Amal said 'we saw' and he fixed to shufna.

agreed.medi_said: Ba'id ma shufna. After we saw...
agreed.amal_said: That. You didn't-- You did-- You need a that here.
agreed.why: A clause after 'we saw' needs enno (that); Amal said you need a 'that' and he added Enna.
agreed.proposed_rule: After a seeing/knowing verb, a full clause is linked with enno (that): ba3ed ma shufna enno tani mat3am kaan nafs el-ishi.

agreed.why: Past description needs kaan; Amal said 'Was, was' and he added kan.
agreed.english: The second restaurant was the same.

agreed.why: Singular for plural 'friends'; Amal said 'Friends' and he switched to sahabik.

agreed.amal_said: No. ... It's definitive. What do you do with it? ... No, sahabak al-thaniyin.
agreed.why: After a definite (possessed) noun the adjective takes el- and agrees in plural; Amal said no and gave sahabak al-thaniyin.

agreed.medi_said: so هداك. No. Yeah. Right? هداك?
agreed.amal_said: شو؟ ... غير عن. What does this mean?
agreed.why: 'These' (plural friends) is هدول, not singular هداك; Amal said شو؟ and prompted, he gave هدول, she said صح.

r1.medi_said: أم خطيبتي، جهزت... الـ ممرّة / جهزت ما...
r1.amal_said: جهزت is like prepared... بس عملت أو طبخت would be a better fit for food.
r1.why: He used جهزت (prepared) for cooking a dish; Amal said عملت/طبخت fit food better (she allowed جهزت 'could be', so soft).
Date 5/10: he said the counting form خمس; Amal recast خمسة عشرة and he repeated it.

r1.medi_said: Because it's mostly like أغلب men most-- no? Uh, أغلب...
r1.amal_said: لا، it's not the first time we discussed this. We never say أغلب من.
r1.why: He put من after أغلب ('most of'); Amal said we never say أغلب من - أغلب links straight to its noun like idafa.

r1.amal_said: نفس never takes ال before it. Al-always after it.
r1.why: He put el- on نفس itself; Amal named the rule: نفس never takes ال, the ال goes on the word after.

r2.amal_said: نفس never takes ال before it. Al-always after it.
r2.why: He put el- on نفس; Amal named the rule that نفس never takes ال before it, only the noun after it does.
r2.proposed_rule: aghlab / nafs are followed by a noun WITH el- and never take el- themselves: aghlab el-naas, nafs el-ashkhaas (not el-nafs, not ashkhaas el-nafs)

r1.amal_said: نفس never takes ال before it always after and it's before the noun.
r1.why: He put نفس after the noun with ال; Amal stated the rule (before the noun, ال after) and he fixed it to نفس الأشخاص.

r2.amal_said: صح. ... نفس never takes ال before it always after and it's before the noun.
r2.why: He put نفس after the noun with el-; Amal said it comes before the noun and never takes ال, he fixed to نفس الأشخاص.
r2.proposed_rule: aghlab / nafs are followed by a noun WITH el- and never take el- themselves: aghlab el-naas, nafs el-ashkhaas (not el-nafs, not ashkhaas el-nafs)

r1.amal_said: Why do you not like forget bisha for example?
r1.why: He used formal قبيحة for ugly; Amal brought up بشعة (the dialect word he learned early) - soft, may be just a comment.

r1.amal_said: No, that's my first day. I want you to say the beginning of my day.
r1.why: He used يومي الأول (my first day) for 'the beginning of my day'; Amal said no and he went to أول يومي.
r1.proposed_rule: أول as an adjective after the noun (يومي الأول) = first; أول in front of a noun with a possessive (أول يومي) = the beginning of it.

r1.amal_said: It doesn't, but it, it takes ak. Sahabak.
r1.why: Speaking of Medi's own friends ('your' m.) needs -ak, he used -ik; Amal stressed 'it takes ak. Sahabak'.

r1.amal_said: What is difference? They are different. ... مختلف أو غير. مختلفين.
r1.why: He used the noun فرق (difference) for 'different' (also at 59:14); Amal said 'what is difference? they are different' and he said مختلف، مختلفين (sheet: different (from) | mu5talef | مختلف).

r2.amal_said: What is difference? They are different. ... مختلف أو غير. مختلفين.
r2.why: فرق is the noun 'difference', not 'different'; Amal said 'What is difference? They are different' and he said مختلفين (sheet: different (from) | mu5talef | مختلف). He first used farq at 59:14.

r2.amal_said: جهزت is like prepared... بس عملت أو طبخت would be a better fit for food.
r2.why: For cooking a dish Amal said جهزت gives 'prepared everything' and عملت or طبخت is the right verb for food.

r2.medi_said: اليوم بلبس بلوزة، أو قميص رسمي
r2.why: Asked what he is wearing today he used the habitual بلبس; the participle لابس fits (B15 not taught yet, filed only).
r2.english: Today I'm wearing a formal white shirt.

r2.proposed_rule: aghlab / nafs are followed by a noun WITH el- and never take el- themselves: aghlab el-naas, nafs el-ashkhaas (not el-nafs, not ashkhaas el-nafs)
